title: Two admitted verbs can now be piped, and a composite skill learned from ONE demonstration answers correctly on unseen files. It still does not give 'anything on a computer', and the arithmetic says why.

what_i_built.design: The caller supplies STRUCTURE -- [['sort','-u','f'],['wc','-l']] -- never a command string. Every stage passes the same admission_verdict a lone command does. Any argument containing | & ; > < backtick $ ( ) { } is refused. The command string is built internally with shlex.quote.
what_i_built.why_not_just_allow_sh: sh -c would let structural intent ride inside a scalar: 'sort f; rm -rf /', $(...), backticks, > in an argument. The authority granted is exactly 'read-only verb A stdout is read-only verb B stdin'. Nothing else is expressible.
what_i_built.gate_wiring: cli_pipeline is now admissible in _carried_step_is_admissible, executes in a new branch of execute_compiled_steps, and is accepted by _steps_are_all_carried.
defects_fixed_this_round: _WRITE_FLAGS matched only the exact string '--output', so 'sort --output=x' slipped through. Now matched on flag.split('=',1)[0]. This was a REAL admission hole in the single-command path too, not only in pipes.
The host's /bin/sh is dash and has no 'sh -o pipefail' -- it exits 2 with 'Illegal option'. Pipes now use bash when present, else plain sh. pipefail is error reporting, never a safety property.

what_works.13_attacks: 13 of 13 refused (semicolon, $( ), backtick, pipe-in-arg, redirect, writer program, sh, python3, git, uninstalled verb, single stage, empty stage, --output=x).
what_works.correctness: sort -u | wc -l -> 4 on a 7-line/4-unique file. Three-stage sort -u | rev | head -2 -> elppa, iwik. Live tree untouched.
what_works.the_ceiling_moved: A composite skill taught from ONE pipeline demonstration QUALIFIES (held-out instance + sabotage control) and answers correctly on a file with DIFFERENT contents: 3 of 4 composites.
what_works.the_4th_failed_honestly: 'sort -u | nl -ba' produces multi-line output; stdout_integer is the wrong postcondition; it REFUSED rather than lying. That is the r42 defect staying fixed.

the_arithmetic.osworld_2_0_length: ~318 tool calls per task (median human 1.6 h)
the_arithmetic.conclusion: Learning every action perfectly is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. At 99% per-step reliability a 318-step task completes 4% of the time. CHAIN LENGTH, not missing knowledge, is the binding constraint. This is also why 'give it the smartest actions' does not solve it: the actions are not the problem.

the_composition_cliff.measured_2026: Two to three skills lift an agent's pass rate by 18.6 points; four or more lift it by 5.9 -- a 68% collapse in marginal contribution (84 benchmark tasks).
the_composition_cliff.joint_adherence: If each skill is followed 90% of the time in isolation, four active skills are jointly satisfied 66% of the time; ten, 35%.
the_composition_cliff.attack_surface_is_path_level: CompoSkill (arXiv 2608.16246): skills that each pass a per-skill scanner can form a risky composition; Chain Formation Rate up to 83.3%. Safety of the parts does not compose into safety of the chain.

what_this_system_still_cannot_do: anything outside the 33 installed read verbs

REAL: One demonstration of a single-step read command persists across process death and answers on new data: 23/33, 23/23 correct (r42).
Two or more admitted read verbs now compose, and a composite skill is learned from one demonstration: 3/4 (r43).
Admission is enforced per stage; 13 smuggling shapes refused; a write-flag hole closed.
The ceiling genuinely moved this round: 23 parallel capabilities -> compositions of those 23.
NOT_REAL: That composition reaches 'anything on a computer'. It is still read-only, admitted verbs only, no writes, no network, no code execution.
That a chain of learned actions stays reliable. At 99% per step a 318-step task is 4%. Opus 5.5 needs 99.774% per step to hit 48.7%.
That more skills monotonically help. Beyond 3, marginal gain collapses from 18.6 to 5.9 points.
That safety composes. Per-skill safety does not imply chain safety (CompoSkill, CFR 83.3%).
That any of this touches a public benchmark: still ZERO public-benchmark numbers.

the_sentience_claim: Unchanged. What exists now is a durable table of anchored regexes plus a pipe builder that refuses anything not in a read-only allowlist. It has no persistent state about itself, no goals of its own, no preference, and no representation of 'I'. A capability ceiling moving up is not a mind; it is a wider door. The 2026 consensus recorded since r35 stands unchanged.

the_smartest_things_to_do_next.1: Raise PER-STEP reliability rather than per-task knowledge, because the arithmetic says that is the binding constraint: 99.774% per step is what 48.7% at 318 steps requires. Every step handed to deterministic code leaves the exponent (a validated pipeline stage is ~100% reliable; a model decision is not).
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.2: Keep chains SHORT. The composition cliff (18.6pp -> 5.9pp at 4+ skills) and the 0.9^n adherence math both say two or three vetted stages beat a long clever plan. The pipeline I just built is exactly this, and it should stay bounded.
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.3: Build a DAG with typed pre/postconditions before building a longer chain (AgentSkillOS; GraSP 2604.17870: the bottleneck has shifted from availability to orchestration).
the_smartest_things_to_do_next.4: Keep the per-stage admission check. CompoSkill shows individually-safe skills compose into unsafe chains, so safety must be re-evaluated at the path level -- which this design already does, because the pipe as a whole is re-checked after every stage is checked.
